author: Oleh Kombaiev
title: Apple: Already Undervalued? - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
I will start with the technical parameters of the stock price dynamics.
The last eight years, the dynamics of Apple ( AAPL ) stock are quite qualitatively (R 2 =0.9) described by the exponential trend (that always looks like a straight line on the graphs with log y-axis):
In September Apple’s actual stock price exceeded this trend by the size of the standard deviation, which meant excess exponential growth. Then the situation changed to the opposite. Now Apple’s actual stock price deviates from this trend by less than the size of the standard deviation, which means more or less a balanced price state:
Apple’s current annual rate of return already is below the mean and is coming nearer to zero. The history of the last five years teaches that the lowering of this indicator below the standard deviation limit is a sign of the bottom. But for this it's not necessary that Apple’s stock price should continue to fall - a sideways trend for the next six months is enough.
So, in the context of the trend and return analysis, Apple's stock looks more or less balanced.
Now let's look at Apple’s current price in terms of its financial performance.
In the last quarter Apple’s annual growth rate of revenue was the best in the last three years. At the same time, the current EV/revenue multiple is the lowest in the last two years, and this formally indicates that Apple is undervalued:
But the long-term relationship between the revenue TTM absolute size and the Apple's capitalization indicates an almost perfectly balanced current state :
Now let’s focus on EBITDA. There are even more interesting relationships here.
Over the last two years Apple’s annual EBITDA growth rate and the EV/EBITDA multiple values have shown a significant relationship, within the bounds of which the EBITDA growth rate in the last quarter deserves a higher EV/EBITDA multiple:
But if we broaden the horizon of the analysis and consider the relationship between the four-year CAGR of EBITDA and the EV/EBITDA multiple over the last 12 years, the result of the last quarter still indicates Apple’s overvalued capitalization, although to a lesser extent than at the beginning of the year:
Finally, the long-term relationship between Apple’s absolute EBITDA TTM and capitalization indicates an almost balanced current price of the company :
The same conclusion is obtained from the analysis of the long-term relationship between Apple’s absolute values of FCF and its capitalization:
Now let's look at Apple's capitalization from the different angle.
In the last quarter Apple's ROE amounted to the historical maximum value . And it's really cool. However, the P/BV multiple remains still higher than its balanced value within the bounds of the relationship between the specified indicators:
But I have to admit that the ROE of Apple is currently the highest compared to those of other FAAAMG companies:
FB Return on Equity (TTM) data by YCharts As a conclusion... At my glance, one should not confidently assert that Apple alread yis undervalued. The drop by 20% relative to the October peak only has led Apple’s capitalization to a balanced state. And in order to become truly undervalued, Apple needs either another wave of decline or a sideways trend for the next five to six months.
Disclosure: I/we have no positions in any stocks mentioned, and no plans to initiate any positions within the next 72 hours.
